changes.change: **Weekly rate is chosen by the person, not by muscle size.** 3 / 5 / 7 % of that muscle's weekly sets, picked each week from the person's state (effort trend, completion, performance, sleep/stress); the coach can override. Every big = 3 % / small = 7 % mapping and the 'focus = one class up' rule are retired.
**10 % per week is a ceiling, not a step.** The person's total weekly resistance sets never rise more than 10 % week over week.

**Release = one whole set per bank unit.** Bank the fraction every week; add a set when the bank reaches 1. The v0 'chunk = round(10 % x current), 1-2 sets' is retired; the chat's 20 → 22 now takes two weeks at 5 % (+1, +1).

**Where a new set goes: the coach's order.** 3-4 exercises per muscle on its day; add to the first exercise in session order, then the next (2/2/2 → 3/2/2 → 3/3/2 → 3/3/3 → 4/3/3); days rotate; small muscles that sit at the end of a session get a bonus exercise; a full big muscle gets a Focus slot. Retires v0's round robin and '<= 2 exercises per muscle per session'.

**Helper credit 0.25** (was 0.5). Dips 0.5 triceps / 0.5 chest; thruster 1.0 quads / 0.5 shoulders; leg curl and leg extension count fully. A 10/10 unilateral set = 1 set, mostly for quads. Athletic patterns (plyos, ballistics, throws, Olympic lifts, sprints, COD) never count toward muscles.

changes.change: **Volume landmarks from the coach.** Start: beginner 10-12, intermediate 15-20, advanced 20+; 15-20 = maintenance to some growth, 20-25 = growth; priority +4-6 (cap about 25-30, 1-2 muscles); pain -30-50 %, machines, or drop the exercise. Research charts are in 12 §2; the tool learns later from users' data.

**Readiness gates follow GEN-05.** EFFORT 9-10 → hold or cut; EFFORT <= 6 → add; 'Felt a PAIN' → swap in category / constrain / drop; v0's per-muscle RED/AMBER/GREEN/EASY gate is replaced by the person-level readiness score of 12 (PROPOSED weights).

**Bilateral : unilateral on a 90/10 ↔ 10/90 scale** by athlete, goal, phase and pain: bodybuilders/powerlifters about 50/50 for the first 2-4 weeks, then 80/20-90/10; field/COD athletes 80-90 % unilateral; in-season minimal bilateral; pain shifts it. Unilateral = health and rotational foundation; bilateral = the driving force. Upper body follows the same logic. Replaces v0's 35-70 % bilateral targets.

**Contralateral / ipsilateral loading is a variable with use cases.** Contralateral pulls you INTO the hip (COD athletes: football, soccer, basketball, tennis; also to build missing range); ipsilateral helps you OUT of the hip (sprint acceleration: ipsilateral step-ups); for bodybuilders/powerlifters both are health accessories, mostly in weeks 1-4.

**Pairing is a variable (new V24).** Same pattern (squat + lunge) drives one muscle harder (high-level, aesthetics); cross pattern (squat + single-leg hinge) keeps bootcamp and general clients fresh. Hip dominant pairs with push, knee dominant with pull, in full body and bootcamps (anterior/posterior split to avoid bleed-over).

**Axial loading once a week (new V25).** One axial squat a week (the other squat exposure = leg press or belt squat); deadlifts also load the spine, so one axial hinge a week. The 'Athletic Performance - Non-Competitive' tab's (BYOP 'JUSTICE LEAGUE', cited JL) Monday front squat + Thursday low-bar back squat is no longer reproduced.

**Variation policy confirmed.** Exercises fixed for a 4-6-week block; between blocks change one or two small variables (grip, stance, implement, ROM, rep range), never all at once; the second weekly exposure of a slot is a different exercise of the same category; A/B lead-lift weeks are optional for clients who want variety, in any program.

**No bands and no variable resistance anywhere.** Bands, reverse bands, chains and weight releasers are out of the generator; banded substitutes removed from every swap ladder (band row, band-assisted pull-up, band chops, banded leg extension, mini bands). The sheet cells stay as OBSERVED record only. V17 is retired; LV-5 is retired.

**Ordering confirmed, BYOP is the reference.** Row before pulldown always; 'the work' first even when vertical; power before strength; isolation first only for a priority muscle; core FIRST by default (movable by the user).
**Supersets are a fatigue/density tool**: short time, advanced clients who need more stimulus, off-season VO2/mitochondrial work, beginners who do not fatigue.

**Session limits.** Resistance-only 5-7 exercises; field athletes off-season up to 10-12 (2 core + 2-4 plyo/ballistic + 2-3 Olympic/power + 3-4 resistance); about 1.5 h (max 2 h) for athletes, bodybuilders, powerlifters, 45-60 min for general/weight loss; unilateral work costs more time. Calves 3 sets every leg day; rear delts their own sets; about 2 core exercises.

**Plan shapes and deloads.** 4-6 weeks = maintenance/transition at about 50-70 % volume; 8 weeks = start hard, 4 adapting + 4 driving; 12 weeks (preferred) = 2-4 acclimation, 4-6 driving, last weeks hardest; repeated cycles start one level higher; week-by-week and yearly modes; deload = about half the sets, lighter; tests by checkbox or none.

**Position zones are rotation biases (Davidson).** Vertical positions (arms down/standing, arms overhead, deep squat) = external-rotation bias; horizontal (hands in front, knee at hip height) = zone 2 = internal-rotation bias, compressive. Level: front-loaded/low = foundational, on the body/horizontal = intermediate, behind/overhead = advanced; machines/cables easier. Zones do NOT apply to plyos. Levels stay theoretical.

**Plyo 'zones' are method stages, not zones**: receive & pause → receive then create → repeated receive/create (name pending; PROPOSED 'Receive-Create stages' RC1-RC3). Unilateral plyos are harder. Plyo vs ballistic is set by the sport's ground-contact time; programs start ballistic and become plyometric.

**Medball weights confirmed**: slams 10-20 lb, overhead throws 6-10 lb, sit-up throws 6-8 lb, passes/rotations light (8-10 lb), lighter for youth/older, never over 20 lb; no medball for aesthetics/bodybuilders except warm-up. Throws have no levels.

**Olympic lifts for everyone in athletic training** (beginners: DB/KB snatches, hex-bar jumps, hang pulls/cleans; intermediate+ full lifts; youth may lift from the floor); the % ramp 75 → 90 with 4 x 8 → 4 x 4 is the strength-plan default. Full lifts are named 'Squat Snatch' / 'Squat Clean' / 'Squat Clean & Jerk'.
**Contrast confirmed**: intermediate+ athletes, off-season, heavy member about 78-85 %, no rest inside the complex.

**Effort and rest confirmed**: 1-3 RIR always; MAX = technical failure only on small-muscle or bodyweight work; MYO only on the last machine/isolation exercise; rest 1-2 min hypertrophy (up to 3), 3-6 min strength; 40-rep sets only as a CrossFit/AMRAP option.

**Equipment answers**: constraint scale 1-5 approved; machines are not ranked (brands differ; hack squat and leg press more constrained than Smith; belt squat avoids axial loading; GHD/reverse hyper if available and felt in the right muscles); older/injured/high-volume clients → constrained machines and never overhead squat, snatch, low-bar squat or depth jumps; client preference may choose between alternatives.

**Levels**: L1 (novice = newby), L2, L3; client level and exercise level stay separate; level up at the end of a block when logs read '8 - That was perfect' or easier with no pain; one algorithm for every model and level.

**Generic names**: 'JUSTICE LEAGUE' was only a marketing name for a weekend-warrior program (non-competitive athletic adults and youth). # reference arithmetic: vol_engine_v1.py (= 12_volume_algorithm_v1 prototype), driven by engine_sim_v4.py
for each week w of the plan:
    if deload_due(w): emit deload(current, factor=0.5); continue        # PER-05; triggers 3.10
    rate = plan_rate if mode == 'static' else readiness_rate(log[w-1])  # VOL-05: one rate for the PERSON (3.3)
    rate = min(rate, phase_cap(plan, w), 0.10)                          # acclimation 3 %, 8-wk weeks 1-4 5 %, ceiling 10 % (UNI-05)
    for m in muscles (priority first, then big, then small):
        r = 0 if m in pain_frozen else (min(rate, 0.03) if priority_running and m not in priority else rate)
        bank[m] += r * weekly_sets[m]                                   # VOL-04: % of weekly sets per muscle
        while bank[m] >= 1 and weekly_sets[m] + 1 <= cap[m]:            # VOL-06: whole sets only
            if total_sets_after_add > 1.10 * total_sets_last_week: break
            if not place_set(m): bank[m] = min(bank[m], 1.99); break    # 3.6 (VOL-07 order, fallbacks)
            bank[m] -= 1
        if weekly_sets[m] >= cap[m]: bank[m] = 0; progress load/reps/intensifiers
    apply_gates(log)                                                     # GEN-05: '10 - I'm done' -1 set; pain protocol
    for each exercise e with no new set: double_progression(e)           # 3.9
    log volume_load(e, w)                                                # tracked, never steered on (VOL-04)
    if block_boundary(w): change 1-2 small variables; rebalance bilateral share  # PER-02, UNI-02

science: Velocity loss inside a set shapes the adaptation [S39]: stopping at 20 % velocity loss gave similar squat strength gains to 40 % (no significant difference) and a better CMJ (+9.5 % vs +3.5 %) with 40 % fewer reps; 40 % gave more hypertrophy and shifted fibres away from type IIX.
Intent produces velocity-specific adaptations even when the bar cannot move fast [S37]; maximal intended velocity nearly doubled bench 1RM gains vs half speed [S38].

Proximity to failure matters for hypertrophy, little for strength [S21]; failure vs 1-2 RIR adds a trivial growth effect at a higher fatigue cost [S20]. The safe place for failure is a high-constraint machine or isolation (10b EQ-3).
Free-weight injuries mostly involve dropped weights [S11]: technical failure on barbell lifts is the risk point.

Plyometric quality: fast SSC contacts ~100-250 ms with small joint excursions [S57]; drop height is the intensity dial, ~30-40 cm optimal by RSI [S58][S59]; landing before reactive work matches 'TAKING IN FORCES' first.
Heavier medballs make the head drift and the spine side-bend, which kills the hip contribution [S54].
RIR scale: RPE 8 = 2 RIR, RPE 9 = 1 RIR (Zourdos 2016, via 03 5.3).

You squat once and probably deadlift once a week (PER-04). (a) May the squat day and the deadlift day be two different days (two spine-loading days a week), or should both sit on the same day? (b) Do single-leg and staggered-stance DB deadlifts, DB RDLs and hack squats count as loading the spine, or only barbell / trap-bar squats and deadlifts?

With helpers at 0.25, squats and lunges give glutes very little credit. You use contralateral loading to help athletes 'get into the hip' when they lack range (CAT-13). Should the generator choose contralateral vs ipsilateral from a simple hip-range screen, or only by sport (COD → contra, sprint start → ipsi)?

Can the tool make a new variant by changing one detail of a library exercise (for example 'Reverse Lunges' → 'Reverse Lunges with the dumbbell in the opposite hand'), or should it only use exercises written in your library?
PER-02 names grip, stance, implement, range of motion and rep range. Are a load-position step (goblet → front squat) and a contra → ipsi swap also 'small variables'?

Is 2-3 s down and fast up your default for hypertrophy? When do you use slow eccentrics: beginners, home clients with light weights, pain?
